# yantrad

> The Yantra control-plane daemon. Every client talks to this and nothing else; no client ever talks
> directly to a managed machine. **Barely implemented** — an axum server with one route and a
> background refresher; the HTTP API is still M4 work. It is an HTTP surface over `yantra-core`, not
> a second copy of the logic.

## Source

- [src/main.rs](src/main.rs): resolves its bind addresses from Tailscale, fails closed, serves `/healthz`, shuts down on SIGTERM.
- [src/refresh.rs](src/refresh.rs): one background task per data class, writing `yantra_core::snapshot::Snapshot`. The interval is a constant, low enough to keep the ssh masters warm. No request path touches ssh.

## What decides its shape

- [ADR-0005](../../docs/adr/0005-core-logic-in-a-library-crate.md): the logic lives in the library; this crate stays thin.
- [ADR-0004](../../docs/adr/0004-rust-for-the-daemon.md): Rust, with axum and tokio. TypeScript belongs to the browser — do not introduce a second runtime here.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): what is already settled, and what to read before starting — including why there is no `--bind` flag.

## Optional

- [tracker.md](tracker.md): seven invariants waiting here for the daemon that does not exist yet — SQLite, scheduling, PTY. None of them exercised by shipped code.
- [../../tracker.md](../../tracker.md): M4 is the milestone that needs this. Open decisions that affect it are listed there.
- [docs/vision.md](../../docs/vision.md): what the daemon is ultimately for.
